canonical_question: Does the 'bimodal grain size distribution' with 70% nanocrystalline grains (<100 nm) directly influence the radiation resistance compared to a fully uniform nanocrystalline or coarse-grained structure?

question_variants.question: Does the 'bimodal grain size distribution' with 70% nanocrystalline grains (<100 nm) directly influence the radiation resistance compared to a fully uniform nanocrystalline or coarse-grained structure?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports a bimodal grain size distribution (70% nanocrystalline, some ultrafine) but does not explicitly state that this specific distribution influences radiation resistance compared to a fully uniform structure or a coarse-grained one. It notes the radiation resistance in this specific sample.

answers.answer: The paper reports a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm). However, it does not provide a direct comparison to a fully uniform nanocrystalline or coarse-grained structure to isolate the influence of the bimodal distribution on radiation resistance.
answers.measurement_outcome: bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm)
answers.mechanism: None specified for bimodal vs uniform comparison
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative data for uniform or coarse-grained structures provided.
evidence_spans: A detailed characterization of the morphology and phase details of the as-deposited HEA films results in a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm) with an underlying single-phase BCC, with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.
